replacement.title: Use the space a forecheck abandons
replacement.objective: Compare a weak-side connection after a forechecker changes responsibility.
replacement.briefing: YOU control a neutral-zone reset in a wide lane. Gold 1 is nearby. Earlier in this rep Gold 2 screened F1; at this freeze Gold 2 has moved toward the middle and is stated to be changing toward D2. The earlier screen is not shown. D2 is across the rink. Recheck whether the changing pressure opens a route to F1. Navy attacks the right net.
cues: Gold 2’s earlier screen is narrated history, not the current passing-line geometry.
Gold 2 is stated to be changing toward D2; no successful pass is established.

questions.prompt: Which opponent is explicitly changing toward D2?

options.text: Gold 2
Gold 4
Gold 1

questions.explanation: The briefing states Gold 2’s change; the still scene only locates the actors at the freeze.

questions.prompt: Which two observations belong in the next pass decision?

options.text: The assumption that a stated movement guarantees an open lane
Whether Gold 1 can disrupt your release
Whether Gold 2 truly leaves F1’s route

questions.explanation: A changed responsibility is a cue to reassess, not proof that the pass succeeds.

questions.prompt: Arrange a read of the changing forecheck.

options.text: Recognize Gold 2’s shift
Check the newly affected forward route
Choose or retain possession based on actual availability

questions.explanation: The carrier may keep or reset the puck if the apparent opening is not real.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a more central connection toward F1.
questions.explanation: The reference changes the angle around Gold 1 and Gold 2. It may also increase pressure, so it is not automatically better.

questions.prompt: Gold 3 drops directly into F1’s route as Gold 2 leaves. What changes?

options.text: Only D2 can now receive under all conditions
Another defender may replace the original coverage
F1 must remain open because Gold 2 moved

questions.explanation: Coverage can transfer between defenders; read the route as a whole rather than one player.

questions.prompt: Explain why moving one forechecker does not necessarily free a pass.
questions.explanation: Another defender, reach, timing or receiver position can still close the connection.

questions.prompt: What should YOU call as Gold 2 changes toward D2?

options.text: Gold 2 is moving; I am checking D2 and F1 before connecting
Use D2 before checking whether the forward route is reachable
The first lane stays open

questions.explanation: The call names the pressure change and both support choices.

questions.prompt: Which two cues decide the regroup connection?

options.text: Gold 2’s new route
F1 or D2’s current visibility
The forecheck label alone

questions.explanation: Pressure route and receiver access decide whether the regroup helps.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to a central connection toward F1.
questions.explanation: The example moves closer to F1 but farther from D2 and closer to Gold 1 and Gold 2. Compare that pressure with the new passing angles; D2 is not guaranteed to remain reachable.

questions.prompt: Gold 3 fills F1’s route after Gold 2 leaves. What should change?
questions.explanation: Name Gold 3 as the new pressure, protect the puck, and use D2 only if the actual lane remains reachable.

replacement.title: A defender rotates low while a forward covers the point
replacement.objective: Understand a declared role exchange without confusing jersey position with current responsibility.
replacement.briefing: F1 controls behind the Gold net. D1 has rotated low on one side. YOU are F3 and the coach has explicitly assigned YOU to cover D1’s vacated point until the exchange ends. D2 remains at the opposite point. Navy attacks Gold’s net and defends Navy’s net. This is a selected-player teaching view; no movement is implied unless stated.
cues: The briefing explicitly assigns the vacated point during the role exchange.

questions.prompt: Which high area has the coach assigned YOU to cover?

options.text: F1’s spot behind the net
The corner beside F2
D1’s vacated point

questions.prompt: Which two checks make that cover useful?

options.text: The opposing exit route if possession changes
The outlet from the low attack
Whether being a forward prevents high support

questions.explanation: Current responsibilities follow the stated exchange, while pressure and possession still govern position.

questions.prompt: Arrange the stated role replacement.

options.text: Confirm D1’s low rotation
Check the vacated point and exit threats
Occupy useful high support and communicate

questions.explanation: This is a team-plan example, not a universal instruction for every offensive rotation.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward the vacated point to illustrate the assigned cover.
questions.explanation: The reference replaces a high role without copying D2’s opposite point. Timing and passing lanes remain conditional.

questions.prompt: F1 loses the puck behind the net. What becomes relevant immediately?

options.text: The assigned high cover and the possible exit route
Only waiting for the planned pass
The assumption that Navy remains on offense

questions.explanation: Recheck the puck state and exit threats while moving into the assigned cover. YOU start inside the zone, so the point is not already covered in this frame.

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between your listed position as F3 and your temporary rink responsibility.
questions.explanation: A forward can fill point support under an explicit exchange; the label does not by itself determine every next action.

questions.prompt: What should YOU communicate about the temporary point cover?

options.text: I am taking the vacated point; call the low rotation
My normal position removes the assignment
D1 covers the point and low space together

questions.explanation: The message states the temporary area and asks for the teammate rotation.

questions.prompt: Which two cues affect your point responsibility?

options.text: The puck carrier’s route
D1’s low rotation
The listed forward role decides the cover without the puck scan

questions.explanation: Carrier and teammate rotation shape the temporary responsibility.

questions.prompt: Move YOU toward the vacated point and compare the route toward F1.
questions.explanation: The example is near the attacking blue line, opposite D2 and farther from F1. Check the low outlet and exit threats; arrival and a clear pass are not established.

questions.prompt: F1 loses the puck behind the net. What do YOU communicate?
questions.explanation: Call the low threat and D1’s rotation, then keep the point connection while the new carrier and lane are identified.

options.text: Gold 2 in the high slot
The planned breakout from a draw Navy did not win
D1’s pressure responsibility

questions.explanation: The stated contingency applies after the actual loss, not the hoped-for outcome.

questions.prompt: Arrange a response to the lost draw.

options.text: Confirm the actual puck owner
Identify the uncovered inside threat
Take the assigned support role and communicate

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare an inside relation to Gold 2 in the high slot.

The draw guarantees the first assignment
D1 owns the puck

questions.prompt: Compare a deeper inside position against Gold 2.

options.text: Travelling from D1 toward YOU
Already controlled by F1
Already sitting still at YOUR feet

questions.prompt: Which two cues should affect the first-touch option?

options.text: A requirement to pass first-time regardless
Whether Gold 1 closes F1’s route
The arriving pass quality

questions.explanation: Preparation enables an early option, but a changed route or difficult reception can require another action.

questions.prompt: Arrange a prepared-reception routine.

options.text: Scan the forward option before arrival
Update the lane and puck quality
Redirect or control according to what remains available

questions.explanation: Repeated scans can overlap with receiving; extra control is not automatically an error.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare a different receiving angle toward F1 and F2.
questions.explanation: The example changes both forward routes and moves farther from the current loose puck. Whether the pass reaches this new point in time is not established; YOU do not yet control it.

questions.prompt: Gold 1 closes F1 completely as the pass arrives. What might be appropriate?

options.text: Pretend the pre-scan picture cannot change
Control or use another checked option
One-touch into F1’s closed lane by rule

questions.prompt: How can a player prepare early without committing too early?

options.text: I am preparing a touch; call if F1 or F2 becomes covered
The planned spot guarantees the reception
Both support lanes remain available after Gold closes one route

The intended puck spot stays current after it drifts

questions.prompt: Gold closes F1 completely as the puck arrives. Explain your branch.
questions.explanation: Protect the first touch and check F2 or a reset. Do not treat the covered target as the only continuation.

replacement.objective: Track two explicitly stated possession changes while preserving useful third-player support.

questions.prompt: Which possession event is the current one?

options.text: Navy still holds the original recovered puck
F2 has scored at the Gold net
Gold 1 has intercepted Navy’s first recovery pass

questions.explanation: The briefing explicitly places the freeze after the second turnover and assigns the puck to Gold 1.

questions.prompt: Choose two details for your third-player response.

options.text: Gold 2’s outlet toward the defending end
D1’s relation to the new carrier
The attacking route planned before the interception as an unchangeable job

questions.explanation: Repeated turnovers require renewed threat and support reads; the earlier plan may be stale.

questions.prompt: Arrange an update after the second turnover.

options.text: Recognize Gold 1’s control
Check pressure and the next outlet
Recover or support the new defensive picture

questions.explanation: This is a role-update routine; no fixed recovery race is certified.

questions.prompt: Move YOU to compare inside support against Gold 2’s outlet.
questions.explanation: The reference changes from advancing support toward defensive help without duplicating D1’s immediate pressure. Other routes may be useful.

questions.prompt: D1 immediately forces Gold 1 to release a loose puck. What should YOU avoid assuming?

options.text: That either team has already secured the new loose puck
That the picture has changed again
That support still matters

questions.explanation: A forced loose touch is another uncertain contest, not automatic possession for Navy.

questions.prompt: Explain how three different puck states in this sequence create different possible jobs for YOU.
questions.explanation: Distinguish Navy’s recovery, Gold’s interception and the hypothetical new loose touch. Tie each to current support and threats.

questions.prompt: What should YOU say after Gold 1 intercepts Navy’s recovery pass?

options.text: Gold 1 has it; I am checking D1’s pressure and Gold 2’s outlet
The old role continues through both turnovers
F2 already controls it

questions.explanation: The call identifies the current Gold possession and the immediate defensive relationships after the second turnover.

questions.prompt: Which two events can change your third-player job?

options.text: D1 wins the puck back
Gold 2 becomes reachable as support for Gold 1
The first Gold possession remains unchanged

questions.explanation: A Navy recovery changes possession; a reachable Gold 2 changes the current attacking threat. Recheck the role under either update.

questions.prompt: Move YOU inside toward Gold 2’s outlet relationship.
questions.explanation: The example moves nearer the middle and closer to Gold 2, but remains farther from Navy’s net than Gold 2. It is an initial recovery comparison, not completed net-side coverage.

questions.prompt: If D1 wins the puck back, how does your third-player job change?
questions.explanation: Confirm Navy control, then compare support for D1 with cover against another turnover. The earlier defensive task against Gold 1 must be updated.
